questions.explanation: After a state such as ある, ば can be followed by a request: {時間|じかん}があれば、{来|き}てください. After an action ({着|つ}く, {帰|かえ}る) or a point in time, a request or an invitation sounds wrong with ば; use たら ({着|つ}いたら, {十時|じゅうじ}になったら, {帰|かえ}ったら).

questions.stem: How is 顔色 read? "顔色がわるいですね。"
questions.explanation: {顔色|かおいろ}: both kanji take their kun'yomi, {顔|かお} + {色|いろ}. 顔色がわるい means "you look pale, you look unwell".

questions.stem: How is 体重 read? "体重が{少|すこ}しふえました。"
questions.explanation: {体重|たいじゅう} (body weight) uses both on'yomi: タイ + ジュウ. Compounds of two kanji usually take on'yomi; the kun'yomi からだ is for 体 on its own.

questions.stem: Which kanji means "neck" (くび)?
questions.explanation: 首 is neck ({首|くび}). 頭 is head (あたま), 顔 face (かお), 自 self. 首 contains 自 with two marks on top, like a head on its neck.

questions.stem: How is 声 read? "{大|おお}きい声で{話|はな}してください。"
questions.explanation: {声|こえ} is a voice: {大|おお}きい{声|こえ}で, in a loud voice. おと ({音|おと}) is a sound, not a voice; セイ is the on'yomi, used in compounds.

questions.stem: Type the ば form of {行|い}く (to go): ___
questions.explanation: {行|い}く is regular in the ば form: く → け + ば, {行|い}けば. (Its irregular forms are only the て and た forms, {行|い}って and {行|い}った.)

questions.stem: Complete: "{何時|なんじ}に ___ いいですか。" (What time should I come?)
questions.explanation: 〜ばいいですか asks what you should do: {何時|なんじ}に{来|く}ればいいですか. The ば form of {来|く}る is くれば.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?

audio.text: くすりをのめば、ねつがさがりますよ。

choices: You should take the medicine after the fever goes down.
The medicine made the fever go down.
The fever will go down if you take the medicine.
Don't take medicine for a fever.
questions.explanation: {薬|くすり}を{飲|の}めば、ねつが{下|さ}がりますよ: if you take the medicine, the fever will go down. The ending {下|さ}がります is non-past, so it's a prediction, not something that already happened.

questions.stem: Listen. How does the speaker feel?

audio.text: もっとはやくねればよかった。

choices: They regret not going to bed earlier.
They are glad they went to bed early.
They plan to go to bed early.
They want the listener to go to bed.
questions.explanation: もっと{早|はや}くねればよかった: I should have gone to bed earlier. 〜ばよかった always looks back with regret.

questions.stem: Listen. When will the speaker go?

audio.text: じかんがあれば、いきます。

choices: Even if they have no time
questions.explanation: {時間|じかん}があれば、{行|い}きます: if I have time, I'll go. あれば is the ば form of ある; "because" would be から, and "even if" 〜ても (lesson 14).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: If you go to bed early, you can get up early.
questions.explanation: {早|はや}くねれば、{朝|あさ}{早|はや}く{起|お}きられます。The condition (ねれば) comes first. ねる is group 2, so its ば form is ねれば; ×ねるば just adds ば to the dictionary form.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: If you walk every day, your body gets stronger.
questions.explanation: {毎日|まいにち}{歩|ある}けば、{体|からだ}が{強|つよ}くなります。{歩|ある}く is group 1: く → け + ば. The adverb form {強|つよ}く goes before なります (becomes strong).

questions.stem: Read: "ねる{前|まえ}にスマホを{見|み}なければ、よくねむれます。それから、{午後|ごご}はコーヒーを{飲|の}まないでください。{夕方|ゆうがた}{少|すこ}し{歩|ある}けば、{体|からだ}もつかれて、すぐねむれますよ。" Which is NOT one of the pieces of advice?
choices: Don't look at your phone before bed.
Don't drink coffee in the afternoon.
Walk a little in the evening.
Take a nap in the afternoon.
questions.explanation: The text advises no phone before bed (スマホを{見|み}なければ), no coffee in the afternoon and a short walk in the evening ({夕方|ゆうがた}{少|すこ}し{歩|ある}けば). A nap (ひるね) isn't mentioned; {午後|ごご} appears only in the coffee advice.

questions.stem: Match each word to its ば form.
questions.explanation: Group 1 {書|か}く → {書|か}けば; group 2 {見|み}る → {見|み}れば; する → すれば; いい uses よ-: よければ (never ×いければ).

questions.stem: What is the たら form of {来|く}る (to come)?
questions.explanation: たら is the た form + ら, and the た form of {来|く}る is {来|き}た, so {来|き}たら (きたら). くたら and こたら use the dictionary and ない form vowels instead.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "___、{家|うち}で{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ましょう。" (If it rains, let's watch a film at home.)
questions.explanation: A noun takes the plain past だった + ら: {雨|あめ}だったら. 〜かったら is for い-adjectives ({高|たか}かったら), and a noun can't take たら directly.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "{駅|えき}に___、{電話|でんわ}してください。" (When you get to the station, please call me.)
questions.explanation: A request after a sure future event needs たら: {着|つ}いたら、{電話|でんわ}してください. と can't take a request after it, and ば after an action verb sounds wrong with one. ×{着|つ}いたと puts a past form before と.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses もし correctly?
choices: もしパスポートをなくしたら、{大使館|たいしかん}にれんらくします。
もし{明日|あした}になったら、{出|で}かけます。
もし{春|はる}になったら、さくらがさきます。
もし{毎朝|まいあさ}{起|お}きたら、{顔|かお}をあらいます。
questions.explanation: もし marks a condition that may or may not happen: losing your passport. Tomorrow and spring are sure to come, and getting up every morning is a routine, so もし doesn't fit them; drop it ({明日|あした}になったら, {春|はる}になると).

questions.stem: What does "{外|そと}に{出|で}たら、{雨|あめ}がふっていました。" mean?
choices: If I go outside, it will rain.
I went outside after it rained.
Please go outside if it rains.
When I went outside, it was raining.
questions.explanation: 〜たら with a past ending tells what you found: when I went out, it was raining. The past is in the last verb (ふっていました), not in the たら, which never shows tense by itself.

questions.stem: Your friend has a headache. Which is a friendly, casual suggestion?
choices: {薬|くすり}を{飲|の}んだらどう？
{薬|くすり}を{飲|の}めばどうでしたか。
{薬|くすり}を{飲|の}んだらいかがでしたか。
questions.explanation: 〜たらどう？ (polite 〜たらどうですか) suggests: why don't you take some medicine? The past endings (でしたか) turn the others into questions about how something was, and と + どう isn't a suggestion pattern.

questions.stem: Someone offers you a plate of biscuits and says "よかったら、どうぞ。" What do they mean?
choices: Please have some, if you like.
If it's good, I'll take it.
questions.explanation: よかったら (from いい: "if it's good for you") means "if you like". It's a polite offer, not a past "it was good" (that would be よかったです).

questions.stem: How is 病院 read? "病院はどこですか。"
questions.explanation: {病院|びょういん}: ビョウ (with a small ょ) + イン. びよういん, with a full-size よ, is a hair salon.

questions.stem: How is 目薬 read? "この目薬を{使|つか}ってください。"
questions.explanation: {目薬|めぐすり} (eye drops): くすり becomes ぐすり as the second part of the compound, the same voicing as こえ → {大声|おおごえ}.

questions.stem: Which kanji is in いしゃ (doctor) and がくしゃ (scholar)?
questions.explanation: 者 (person): {医者|いしゃ}, {学者|がくしゃ}. 都 and 暑 contain 者 as a part, but they're different kanji (capital, hot); 着 is "wear, arrive".

questions.stem: How is 帰国 read? "{来週|らいしゅう}、帰国します。"
questions.explanation: {帰国|きこく}: two on'yomi, キ + コク. The kun'yomi かえ(る) is for the verb {帰|かえ}る.

questions.stem: Type the たら form of {飲|の}む (to drink): ___
questions.explanation: The た form of {飲|の}む is {飲|の}んだ (む → んだ), so the たら form is {飲|の}んだら.

questions.stem: Complete: "{病院|びょういん}に ___ どうですか。" (Why don't you go to the hospital?)
questions.explanation: 〜たらどうですか: {病院|びょういん}に{行|い}ったらどうですか. {行|い}く has the irregular た form {行|い}った, so the たら form is {行|い}ったら.

questions.stem: Listen. When will the speaker call?

audio.text: にほんについたら、でんわします。

questions.explanation: {日本|にほん}に{着|つ}いたら、{電話|でんわ}します: when I arrive in Japan, I'll call. たら puts the call after the arrival.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker asking?

audio.text: どうしたらいいですか。

questions.explanation: どうしたらいいですか means the same as どうすればいいですか: what should I do? "What happened?" would be どうしたんですか.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the doctor say?

audio.text: ねつがさがったら、だいじょうぶですよ。

choices: The fever went down, so you're fine.
If you're fine, the fever will go down.
You can't travel because of the fever.
You'll be fine once your fever goes down.
questions.explanation: ねつが{下|さ}がったら、だいじょうぶですよ: once the fever has gone down, you'll be fine. たら isn't past, so it doesn't say the fever has already gone down.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: If you lose your passport, contact the embassy.
questions.explanation: パスポートをなくしたら、{大使館|たいしかん}にれんらくしてください。A request follows, so the condition needs たら; なくすと can't be followed by 〜てください.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Today, when I finish work, I'll go to the hospital.
questions.explanation: {今日|きょう}は{仕事|しごと}が{終|お}わったら、{病院|びょういん}に{行|い}きます。The たら clause (when work finishes) comes before the main clause. {今日|きょう}は can open the sentence or the main clause.

questions.stem: Read: "オリバーさんは{旅行|りょこう}{中|ちゅう}にかぜをひきました。{病院|びょういん}に{行|い}ったら、{医者|いしゃ}は「ねつが{下|さ}がったら、ひこうきに{乗|の}ってもだいじょうぶです」と{言|い}いました。{薬|くすり}を{飲|の}んだら、つぎの{日|ひ}にはねつが{下|さ}がりました。" Which is true?
choices: The doctor told Oliver not to fly at all.
Oliver took the medicine and his fever went down the next day.
Oliver's fever went up after he took the medicine.
questions.explanation: {薬|くすり}を{飲|の}んだら、つぎの{日|ひ}にはねつが{下|さ}がりました: after he took the medicine, the fever went down the next day. The doctor said flying would be fine once the fever went down, not that he mustn't fly.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly says "If I had a lot of money, I'd like to travel round the world"?
choices: お{金|かね}がたくさんあると、{世界|せかい}{旅行|りょこう}がしたいです。
お{金|かね}がたくさんあったと、{世界|せかい}{旅行|りょこう}がしたいです。
お{金|かね}がたくさんあって、{世界|せかい}{旅行|りょこう}がしたいです。
お{金|かね}がたくさんあったら、{世界|せかい}{旅行|りょこう}がしたいです。
questions.explanation: A wish (〜たい) after a hypothetical condition takes たら: あったら. と can't be followed by a wish, ×あったと isn't a form, and the て form あって gives "I have a lot of money and want to travel", not "if".

questions.stem: 「カメラを{買|か}いたいんです。」 Which reply uses なら correctly?
choices: カメラなら、{駅|えき}の{前|まえ}の{店|みせ}が{安|やす}いですよ。
カメラだなら、{駅|えき}の{前|まえ}の{店|みせ}が{安|やす}いですよ。
カメラたら、{駅|えき}の{前|まえ}の{店|みせ}が{安|やす}いですよ。
カメラと、{駅|えき}の{前|まえ}の{店|みせ}が{安|やす}いですよ。
questions.explanation: なら takes up the topic the other person raised: "if it's a camera (you want)…". Nouns take なら directly, with no だ (×カメラだなら); a noun can't take たら, and カメラと means "a camera and…".

questions.stem: Advice for before a trip: "{日本|にほん}に___、{日本語|にほんご}を{少|すこ}し{勉強|べんきょう}してください。" (If you're going to Japan, study a little Japanese.)
questions.explanation: The studying should happen before the trip, so it's なら: {行|い}くなら (if you're going to go). {行|い}ったら would mean "once you're in Japan". と and ば after an action can't take a request like this.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "___、{買|か}いたいです。" (I want to buy it even if it's expensive.)
questions.explanation: 〜ても is the て form + も. The て form of {高|たか}い is {高|たか}くて, so "even if it's expensive" is {高|たか}くても.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "___、{分|わ}かります。" (Even a child can understand it.)
questions.explanation: Nouns and な-adjectives take でも: {子|こ}どもでも (even a child). It comes from the て form of です/だ, で + も.

questions.stem: What does "いくら{食|た}べても、{太|ふと}りません。" mean?
choices: If I eat a lot, I'll put on weight.
I eat a lot, so I'm getting fat.
However much I eat, I don't put on weight.
questions.explanation: いくら〜ても is "no matter how much": however much I eat, I don't gain weight. いくら here isn't the price question "how much?", because 〜ても follows.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "この{図書館|としょかん}は、___。" (Anyone can use this library.)
choices: だれでも{使|つか}えます
questions.explanation: だれでも + a positive verb is "anyone". だれも goes with a negative (no one), and だれか is "someone".

questions.stem: Which sentence says "I've only got 1,000 yen" (and it isn't enough)?
choices: {千円|せんえん}しかあります。
{千円|せんえん}だけありません。
{千円|せんえん}しかありません。
{千円|せんえん}ばかりあります。
questions.explanation: しか always takes a negative verb: {千円|せんえん}しかありません. ×しかあります is a common mistake; {千円|せんえん}だけありません would mean something like "just 1,000 yen is missing"; ばかり is "nothing but" and doesn't fit an amount like this.

questions.stem: A shop assistant asks "{何|なに}かおさがしですか。" You're just looking. What do you say?
choices: いいえ、{見|み}るしかです。
いいえ、{見|み}るだけです。
いいえ、{見|み}るばかりです。
いいえ、{見|み}てばかりです。
questions.explanation: {見|み}るだけです: I'm just looking. しか needs a negative verb, and ばかり (nothing but) would sound like a complaint about yourself.

questions.stem: How does the speaker feel in "{弟|おとうと}はゲームばかりしています。"?
choices: Pleased: the brother has just started a game.
Neutral: the brother plays one game only.
Surprised: the brother never plays games.
Critical: the brother plays games and does nothing else.
questions.explanation: Nばかり is "nothing but N", and it usually sounds like a complaint: my brother does nothing but play games. "One game only" would be {一|ひと}つだけ.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I've just eaten"?
questions.explanation: 〜たばかり (lesson 10) is "have just done": {食|た}べたばかりです. 〜てばかりいる is "does nothing but": I do nothing but eat.

questions.stem: How is 図書館 read? "図書館で{本|ほん}を{借|か}ります。"
questions.explanation: {図書館|としょかん}: 図 is ト here, not ズ as in {地図|ちず}. 書 is ショ (short), not しょう.

questions.stem: How is 銀行 read? "銀行でお{金|かね}を{下|お}ろします。"
questions.explanation: {銀行|ぎんこう}: ギン (silver) + コウ. きん is gold ({金|きん}), the kanji on the left of 銀.

questions.stem: How is 売り場 read? "くつ売り場は{二|に}かいです。"
questions.explanation: {売|う}り{場|ば}: the kun'yomi of 売 (う(る)) + ば. It means a sales section or counter: くつ{売|う}り{場|ば}, the shoe department.

questions.stem: How is 特急 read? "特急に{乗|の}りました。"
questions.explanation: {特急|とっきゅう} (limited express): トク shortens to とっ before the k sound of キュウ, as in {出発|しゅっぱつ}.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker recommending?

audio.text: きょうとなら、あきがいいですよ。

questions.explanation: {京都|きょうと}なら、{秋|あき}がいいですよ: if it's Kyoto, autumn is good. なら takes up Kyoto as the topic, and the advice follows.

questions.stem: Listen. How can you pay at this shop?

audio.text: このみせは、げんきんしかつかえません。

questions.explanation: げんきんしか{使|つか}えません: you can only use cash. The negative verb goes with しか and doesn't mean "not cash".

questions.stem: Listen and type what you hear, in hiragana: ___

audio.text: いつでもいいですよ。

questions.explanation: いつでもいいですよ: any time is fine. いつ + でも is "any time at all".

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: If you're going to Kyoto, autumn is the best time.
questions.explanation: {京都|きょうと}に{行|い}くなら、{秋|あき}がいちばんいいですよ。The なら clause comes first; いちばん goes right before the adjective it strengthens.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: However hard I look, the price isn't written anywhere.
questions.explanation: いくらさがしても、ねだんが{書|か}いてありません。いくら and 〜ても belong together, and 〜てある (lesson 8) ends the sentence. ねだんが can also come first: ねだんが、いくらさがしても{書|か}いてありません.

questions.stem: Read the notice: "みどり{映画館|えいがかん}：{上映|じょうえい}は{毎日|まいにち}10:00、14:00、19:00（{月曜日|げつようび}は19:00だけ）。{水曜日|すいようび}は、だれでも1,200{円|えん}。{特別|とくべつ}{上映|じょうえい}のチケットは、{上映|じょうえい}の{日|ひ}に{映画館|えいがかん}でしか{買|か}えません。" Which is true?
choices: There is no showing on Mondays.
Tickets can be bought online the day before.
Only students pay 1,200 yen on Wednesdays.
On Mondays there is only one showing.
questions.explanation: {月曜日|げつようび}は19:00だけ: on Mondays, only the 19:00 showing. Tickets can be bought only at the cinema on the day ({映画館|えいがかん}でしか{買|か}えません), and on Wednesdays it's 1,200 yen for everyone (だれでも).

questions.stem: Which is the correct polite "must go"?
choices: {行|い}かなければなりません
{行|い}かないければなりません
{行|い}かなくてもなりません
questions.explanation: Must = the ない form's ば form ({行|い}かなければ) + なりません ("it won't do"). The ending is negative, so ×なります is wrong; ×{行|い}かないければ adds ければ without dropping い.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "{明日|あした}も___。" (I have to come tomorrow too.)
questions.explanation: The ない form of {来|く}る is {来|こ}ない, so "must come" is {来|こ}なければなりません. {来|こ}なければいいです means "it's best if you don't come".

questions.stem: 「{写真|しゃしん}を{持|も}って{来|こ}なければなりませんか。」 How do you answer "No, you don't have to"?
choices: いいえ、{持|も}って{来|き}てはいけません。
いいえ、{持|も}って{来|こ}なければいけません。
いいえ、{持|も}って{来|こ}なくてもいいです。
いいえ、{持|も}って{来|き}てもいいです。
questions.explanation: The "no" to a must-question is 〜なくてもいいです (you don't have to). 〜てはいけません means "you mustn't bring it", a ban, and 〜てもいいです means "you may bring it".

questions.stem: A friend says "I've got to go" casually: "もう___。"
questions.explanation: なければ shortens to なきゃ in casual speech: もう{行|い}かなきゃ. The casual 〜なくちゃ comes from なくては, so ×{行|い}かないちゃ is wrong; {行|い}けなきゃ uses the potential (I must be able to go).

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "{今日|きょう}は{写真|しゃしん}を{出|だ}す___。" (There's no need to hand in a photo today.)
choices: ひつようはありません
questions.explanation: Dictionary form + ひつようはありません: there's no need to. ひつようがあります says the opposite (you need to), and ひつよう isn't an object of する.

questions.stem: Read the notice: "{用紙|ようし}は{黒|くろ}いボールペンで{書|か}いてください。えんぴつで{書|か}いてはいけません。{本人|ほんにん}が{来|こ}られない{場合|ばあい}は、{家族|かぞく}でもかまいません。{写真|しゃしん}は{出|だ}すひつようはありません。" Which is true?
choices: A family member may come instead of you.
You must hand in a photo.
Only you can come; nobody else may.
questions.explanation: {本人|ほんにん}が{来|こ}られない{場合|ばあい}は、{家族|かぞく}でもかまいません: if you can't come, a family member is fine. Pencil isn't allowed (〜てはいけません), and no photo is needed (ひつようはありません).

questions.stem: Who would naturally say "{早|はや}くねなさい。"?
choices: A shop assistant to a customer
questions.explanation: 〜なさい is a firm command from someone with authority: a parent to a child, a teacher to pupils. To a teacher, a customer or a boss it would be rude; they'd hear 〜てください or more polite forms.

questions.stem: Painted on the road before a crossing you see {止|と}まれ. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: {止|と}まれ is the imperative of {止|と}まる (group 1: る → れ): Stop! "Don't stop" would be {止|と}まるな, with な after the dictionary form.

questions.stem: Which is the blunt "Don't touch!" you might see on a warning sign?
questions.explanation: Dictionary form + な is the blunt "don't": さわるな. さわれ is the imperative "touch!", and the other two ask you to touch it.

questions.stem: What is the imperative of {来|く}る (to come)?
questions.explanation: {来|く}る → こい (come here!) is irregular. くれ is the imperative of くれる (give me), きろ is the imperative of {着|き}る (to wear), and くろ isn't a verb form.

questions.stem: How is 東京都 read?
questions.explanation: {東京都|とうきょうと}: トウ + キョウ + ト, the metropolis of Tokyo. 都 is ツ only in a few words such as {都合|つごう}.

questions.stem: How is 正しい read? "正しいものをえらびなさい。"
questions.explanation: {正|ただ}しい (correct) uses the kun'yomi ただ(しい). セイ and ショウ are on'yomi, for compounds such as {正午|しょうご}.

questions.stem: How is 手紙 read? "{母|はは}に手紙を{書|か}きました。"
questions.explanation: {手紙|てがみ} (letter): かみ (paper) becomes がみ as the second half of the word.

questions.stem: Which kanji means "prefecture"?
questions.explanation: 県 (けん): {山口県|やまぐちけん}. 市 is city, 都 is capital or metropolis ({東京都|とうきょうと}), 京 capital ({東京|とうきょう}, {京都|きょうと}).

questions.stem: Complete: "{名前|なまえ}を ___ なりません。" (I have to write my name.)
questions.explanation: {書|か}かない → {書|か}かなければ + なりません. Start from the ない form, then change ない to なければ.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the official say about the seal (はんこ)?

audio.text: はんこはなくてもいいです。

questions.explanation: はんこはなくてもいいです: it's fine even without a seal, so you don't need one. なくても comes from ない (there isn't), not from a ban.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker mean?

audio.text: もういかなきゃ。

questions.explanation: もう{行|い}かなきゃ is casual for もう{行|い}かなければいけません: I must go now. なきゃ sounds negative, but it's "must".

questions.stem: Listen. How should you fill in the form?

audio.text: くろいボールペンでかいてください。

questions.explanation: {黒|くろ}いボールペンで{書|か}いてください: please write in black ballpoint pen. で marks what you write with.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
tiles: {十四日|じゅうよっか}のうちに
accept: {十四日|じゅうよっか}のうちに
questions.prompt: When you move house, you have to go to the city office within fourteen days.
questions.explanation: ひっこしたら、{十四日|じゅうよっか}のうちにしやくしょに{行|い}かなければなりません。The たら clause comes first and なければなりません ends the sentence; the time and the place can swap.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: You don't have to bring a photo today.
questions.explanation: {今日|きょう}は{写真|しゃしん}を{持|も}って{来|こ}なくてもいいです。〜なくてもいい is "don't have to". {来|き}ては would start 〜てはいけない (mustn't), the opposite.

questions.stem: Fill the blank: "{用紙|ようし}は、えんぴつで___ほうがいいですよ。" (You'd better not fill in the form in pencil.)
questions.explanation: Advice against is the plain ない form + ほうがいい: {書|か}かないほうがいい. ×{書|か}かなかったほうがいい is a common mistake: only the positive uses the た form ({書|か}いたほうがいい, you'd better write it), and that says the opposite.

questions.stem: Your teacher looks very tired. Which is the most suitable thing to say?
choices: {先生|せんせい}、{休|やす}みなさい。
{先生|せんせい}、{休|やす}まなければなりません。
{先生|せんせい}、{少|すこ}し{休|やす}んだほうがいいと{思|おも}います。
questions.explanation: 〜たほうがいい is advice, and と{思|おも}います softens it for someone above you. 〜なさい is a command from above, {休|やす}め is the blunt imperative, and 〜なければなりません states a rule ("you must"), all too strong for a teacher.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: You'd better go to the hospital soon.
questions.explanation: {早|はや}く{病院|びょういん}に{行|い}ったほうがいいですよ。Advice to do something is the た form + ほうがいい; the た form isn't past here. {行|い}かなかった is never used before ほうがいい (better not is {行|い}かないほうがいい). {早|はや}く and {病院|びょういん}に can swap.

questions.stem: What does {地震|じしん} mean?
questions.explanation: {地震|じしん} is an earthquake. Evacuation is {避難|ひなん}, a tsunami つなみ, a fire {火事|かじ}.

questions.stem: A sign says {避難|ひなん}{場所|ばしょ}. What is it?
questions.explanation: {避難|ひなん}{場所|ばしょ} is an evacuation area, usually an open space like a park. An emergency exit is ひじょうぐち.

questions.stem: Which number do you call for an ambulance in Japan?
questions.explanation: 119 is for fire and ambulance (きゅうきゅうしゃ). 110 is the police. 118 is the coast guard (emergencies at sea) and 117 the speaking clock.

questions.stem: An announcement says "ゆれたら、つくえの{下|した}に{入|はい}ってください。" When should you get under a desk?
questions.explanation: ゆれたら: when it shakes. たら here is "when" for the moment the shaking starts; "after it stops" would be ゆれがおさまったら.

questions.stem: When you call 119, the operator asks "{火事|かじ}ですか、きゅうきゅうですか。" What are they asking?
choices: Is it a fire, or do you need an ambulance?
Is anyone hurt in the fire?
questions.explanation: The first question at 119 sorts the call: {火事|かじ} (a fire) or きゅうきゅう (a medical emergency, an ambulance).

questions.stem: Someone shouts "にげろ！" What should you do?
questions.explanation: にげろ is the imperative of にげる (group 2: る → ろ): run away, get out! In an emergency a short command isn't rude.

questions.stem: In the school evacuation rule おかしも, what does も stand for?
questions.explanation: おかしも: おさない (don't push), かけない (don't run), しゃべらない (don't talk), もどらない (don't go back).

questions.stem: You are near the sea when a strong earthquake hits. What is the usual advice?
choices: Go down to the beach to look at the waves.
Wait for the shaking to repeat before moving.
Drive along the coast road to get home.
Go to high ground at once.
questions.explanation: A tsunami can follow a strong earthquake near the coast, so the advice is to go to high ground immediately (すぐ {高|たか}い{所|ところ}ににげる), not to look at the sea or stay on the coast.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the announcement say?

audio.text: エレベーターはつかわないでください。

questions.explanation: エレベーターは{使|つか}わないでください: please don't use the lifts. 〜ないでください is "please don't".

questions.stem: Listen. When should you go outside?

audio.text: ゆれがおさまったら、そとにでてください。

choices: Only if there is a fire
questions.explanation: ゆれがおさまったら、{外|そと}に{出|で}てください: once the shaking has died down, go outside. たら puts going out after the shaking stops.

questions.stem: Type the word for "ambulance" in hiragana: ___
questions.explanation: きゅうきゅうしゃ: two long きゅう beats, then しゃ. Call 119 for one.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {火事|かじ} is a fire, つなみ a tsunami, ひなん evacuation, ゆれる to shake. "To run away" is にげる.

questions.stem: Within how many days of moving in do you have to register at your new city office?
questions.explanation: The moving-in notification ({転入|てんにゅう}とどけ) is due within 14 days of moving in.

questions.stem: A form has a box labelled 生年月日. What do you write there?
questions.explanation: {生年月日|せいねんがっぴ} is the date of birth: the year, month and day you were born (生, born).

questions.stem: Which date of birth is written in the usual Japanese order?
questions.explanation: Japanese dates go from the biggest unit to the smallest: year, month, day.

questions.stem: What do you write in a box marked フリガナ?
choices: The reading of your name, in katakana
questions.explanation: フリガナ is the reading of the name written above or beside it, in katakana when the box is labelled in katakana.

questions.stem: Your ticket says 28. You hear "{二十八|にじゅうはち}ばんのかた、{三|さん}ばんまどぐちへどうぞ。" What do you do?
questions.explanation: {二十八|にじゅうはち}ばんのかた is "the person with number 28", and {三|さん}ばんまどぐちへどうぞ "please go to window 3".

questions.stem: Which address is written in the Japanese order?
choices: 3-5-2{中町|なかまち}{山川市|やまかわし}{山口県|やまぐちけん}
{山川市|やまかわし}{山口県|やまぐちけん}{中町|なかまち}3-5-2
{山口県|やまぐちけん}{山川市|やまかわし}{中町|なかまち}3-5-2
{中町|なかまち}3-5-2{山口県|やまぐちけん}{山川市|やまかわし}
questions.explanation: Addresses start with the biggest unit: prefecture ({県|けん}), city ({市|し}), district, then the block numbers.

questions.stem: You are moving to another city. What must you do at your old city office before you leave?
choices: Register the move in ({転入|てんにゅう})
Report the move out ({転出|てんしゅつ})
Nothing: only the new city needs to know
questions.explanation: Before you leave, you report the move out ({転出|てんしゅつ}とどけ) at the old town; the move in ({転入|てんにゅう}) is registered at the new one.

questions.stem: Why does the official ask to see your residence card (ざいりゅうカード) when you register a move?
choices: To keep it until you leave Japan
To give you a new card
To write your new address on the back
questions.explanation: The city office writes the new address on the back (うら) of the residence card; you get it back at once.

questions.stem: Listen. Which part of the form do you fill in?

audio.text: ふといせんのなかだけきにゅうしてください。

choices: Only the part inside the thick lines
Only the back of the form
questions.explanation: {太|ふと}いせんの{中|なか}だけきにゅうしてください: fill in only the part inside the thick lines. だけ limits it to that part; the rest is for the office.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the official say about your date of birth?

audio.text: せいれきでもかまいません。

choices: You must use the era name.
You don't have to write it.
questions.explanation: せいれきでもかまいません: the Western calendar year is fine too. 〜でもかまいません means "… is also all right".

questions.stem: Type the word for "counter, service window" (at an office) in hiragana: ___
questions.explanation: まどぐち: まど (window) + くち (opening), with く voiced to ぐ.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {転入|てんにゅう} is moving in, {転出|てんしゅつ} moving out, {年金|ねんきん} a pension, せいべつ the sex box on a form. "Date of birth" is {生年月日|せいねんがっぴ}.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "It looks delicious"?
questions.explanation: With "looks", an い-adjective drops its final い before そう: おいし + そう. おいしいそうです keeps the い, which makes it lesson 17's hearsay ("I hear it's delicious").

questions.stem: このレストラン、___ですね。 (This restaurant looks good.)
questions.explanation: いい is irregular: it becomes よ- and adds さ, giving よさそう. いいそう is hearsay ("I hear it's good"), and よそう drops the さ that いい and ない need (なさそう works the same way).

questions.stem: The sky has gone dark. Which sentence means "It looks like it's going to rain"?
questions.explanation: For "looks like it will", そう goes on the ます stem: ふります → ふりそう. ふるそうです (plain form + そう) is hearsay, "I hear it will rain", and ふったそうです is "I hear it rained". ようです never joins the ます stem.

questions.stem: Complete with the "looks" form of ない: もう{時間|じかん}が___です。 (It looks like there's no time left.)
questions.explanation: ない (there isn't) works like いい: it adds さ before そう, giving なさそう. ないそう would be hearsay ("I hear there isn't").

questions.stem: ___ケーキですね。 (That's a delicious-looking cake.)
questions.explanation: 〜そう behaves like a な-adjective, so before a noun it takes な: おいしそうなケーキ. おいしそうに is for a verb (おいしそうに{食|た}べる), and hearsay そう (おいしいそう) can't come before a noun at all.

questions.stem: {弟|おとうと}は___ラーメンを{食|た}べています。 (My brother is eating his ramen with obvious enjoyment.)
questions.explanation: Before a verb, 〜そう takes に, like any な-adjective used as an adverb: おいしそうに{食|た}べる, "eat looking as if it's delicious". おいしそうな goes before a noun, and の never follows そう.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Grandma looked well"?
choices: おばあさんは{元気|げんき}だそうでした。
おばあさんは{元気|げんき}なそうでした。
おばあさんは{元気|げんき}そうでした。
おばあさんは{元気|げんき}のそうでした。
questions.explanation: A な-adjective takes そう directly, with nothing between: {元気|げんき}そう, past {元気|げんき}そうでした. {元気|げんき}だそう is hearsay ("I hear she's well") and can't be put in the past like this; な and の don't go before そう.

questions.stem: You're holding an apple that is plainly bright red. Which is the natural thing to say?
choices: このりんごは{赤|あか}そうですね。
このりんごは{赤|あか}いですね。
このりんごは{赤|あか}いそうですね。
このりんごは{赤|あか}のようですね。
questions.explanation: 〜そう is a guess from appearance, so it sounds odd for something you can plainly see: the apple simply is {赤|あか}い. {赤|あか}いそう would be hearsay, and {赤|あか}のよう ("seems to be red, the colour") isn't natural here either.

questions.stem: What does かわいそうな{犬|いぬ} mean?
choices: a dog people say is cute
questions.explanation: かわいそう is a word of its own: "poor thing, pitiful". It isn't the "looks" form of かわいい; for a dog that looks cute, just say かわいい{犬|いぬ}.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "This doesn't look tasty"?
choices: これはおいしくなさそうです。
これはおいしいそうじゃないです。
これはおいしなさそうです。
これはおいしそうないです。
questions.explanation: Make the negative おいしくない, then change ない to なさそう: おいしくなさそう. おいしそうじゃない would also work, but おいしいそうじゃない mixes in hearsay, and the other two aren't real forms (おいしなさそう skips the く of おいしくない).

questions.stem: What does {雨|あめ}はやみそうにありません。 mean?
choices: I hear the rain won't stop.
It looks like it will stop raining soon.
The rain doesn't look like stopping.
questions.explanation: やむ (stop, of rain) → ます stem やみ + そう, and 〜そうにない / そうにありません is the negative for verbs: "doesn't look like it will". Hearsay would be やまないそうです.

questions.stem: Match each word to its "looks" (そう) form.
questions.explanation: い-adjectives drop い (おいしそう); いい and ない add さ (よさそう, なさそう); な-adjectives add そう directly ({元気|げんき}そう). いいそう and ないそう are hearsay forms.

questions.stem: Listen. What is about to happen?

audio.text: にくがこげそう！

choices: The meat is going to burn.
questions.explanation: にくがこげそう: こげる (burn, of food) → ます stem こげ + そう, "looks like it's going to burn". "Has burned" would be こげた, and "tender" is やわらかそう.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?

audio.text: このカレーはからそうですね。

choices: I hear this curry is spicy.
questions.explanation: からそう: からい (spicy) − い + そう, "looks spicy". Hearsay would keep the い (からいそう), and "sweet" is あまい.

questions.stem: Listen and type what you hear, in hiragana: ___

audio.text: おいしそう

questions.explanation: おいしそう (looks delicious): おいしい − い + そう. The そう has a long vowel: so-o.

questions.stem: How is 野菜 read? {八百屋|やおや}で野菜を{買|か}いました。
questions.explanation: 野菜 is やさい (vegetables), with the on'yomi of both kanji: ヤ + サイ. の and な are their kun'yomi, used in other words ({菜|な}の{花|はな}). {八百屋|やおや} is a greengrocer.

questions.stem: Which kanji means "fish"?
questions.explanation: 魚 (さかな) is a picture of a fish: head, scaly body and tail. 肉 is meat, 牛 is cow and 菜 is greens.

questions.stem: How is 牛肉 read?
questions.explanation: 牛肉 (beef) uses on'yomi: ギュウ + ニク, ぎゅうにく. うし is the animal on its own ({牛|うし}), and ぎゅうにゅう is milk, which this course writes in kana.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: The sky is dark, so it looks like it'll rain any moment.
questions.explanation: The reason comes first ({空|そら}が{暗|くら}いから), then the prediction. そう goes on the ます stem ふり, not on the dictionary form ふる. {今|いま}にも can come before or after {雨|あめ}が.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: My little brother is eating his ramen with obvious enjoyment.
questions.explanation: おいしそうに describes how he eats, so it goes before the verb, either before or after the object. The adverb form is そうに; おいしいそうに mixes in the hearsay form and isn't a word.

questions.stem: Complete with hearsay そう: あの{店|みせ}のラーメンはとても___です。 (I hear the ramen at that place is really good.)
questions.explanation: Hearsay そうだ follows the full plain form, so the い stays: おいしいそうです. おいしそうです would mean "it looks good".

questions.stem: {明日|あした}は{雨|あめ}___そうです。 (I hear it'll rain tomorrow.)
questions.explanation: After a noun, hearsay そうだ needs the plain だ: {雨|あめ}だそうです. Without だ, {雨|あめ}そう isn't a word at all (lesson 16's そう can't follow nouns); な and の belong to ようだ.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I hear it was very cold yesterday"?
choices: きのうはとても{寒|さむ}いそうでした。
きのうはとても{寒|さむ}そうでした。
きのうはとても{寒|さむ}かったようでした。
きのうはとても{寒|さむ}かったそうです。
questions.explanation: The past goes inside, on the adjective: {寒|さむ}かった + そうです. そうだ itself never changes, so ×{寒|さむ}いそうでした is wrong. {寒|さむ}そうでした is "it looked cold", which is lesson 16's そう.

questions.stem: Which one means "I hear it's quiet"?
questions.explanation: A な-adjective keeps だ before hearsay そうだ: しずかだそうです. しずかそうです, with nothing between, is "it looks quiet".

questions.stem: What does このケーキ、おいしいそうですよ。 mean?
choices: I hear this cake is delicious.
This cake seems delicious, judging by the smell.
questions.explanation: The full form おいしい before そう marks hearsay: someone told you. "Looks delicious" would be おいしそう, with the い dropped.

questions.stem: てんきよほう___、{明日|あした}は{寒|さむ}くなるそうです。
questions.explanation: 〜によると names the source of what you heard: "according to the forecast". について means "about", and によって (by, depending on) and のために (for) don't name a source.

questions.stem: You pass on a message to your teacher: Kenta said he can't come tomorrow. Which is best?
choices: けんたさんは{明日|あした}{来|こ}られないって。
けんたさんは{明日|あした}{来|こ}られないと{言|い}っていました。
けんたさんは{明日|あした}{来|こ}られませんと{言|い}いますか。
けんたさんは{明日|あした}{来|こ}られないそうな{言|い}いました。
questions.explanation: 〜と{言|い}っていました is the polite way to pass on what someone said. 〜って is right in meaning but casual, so not for a teacher; 〜と{言|い}いますか asks a question ("does he say…?"), and 〜そうな{言|い}いました is ungrammatical.

questions.stem: Listen. A friend says this to you. What does she mean?

audio.text: あした、あめだって。

questions.explanation: Sentence-final って is casual hearsay: "they say", "apparently". "It looks like rain" would be {雨|あめ}がふりそう, and a question would be {雨|あめ}？

questions.stem: Do you know a restaurant called Midori? 「みどり」___レストランを{知|し}っていますか。
questions.explanation: 〜という + noun is "a … called": 「みどり」というレストラン. ような is "like", and と{言|い}った would mean "that said", not "called". Hearsay そう can't come before a noun.

questions.stem: Someone asks {夕立|ゆうだち}って{何|なん}ですか。 What are they doing?
choices: Asking what the word yuudachi means
Saying they heard about a yuudachi
Saying it looks like a yuudachi
Telling someone a yuudachi is coming
questions.explanation: Here って marks a topic being asked about: "what's this thing called yuudachi?" It isn't hearsay here, because it's followed by a question about the word itself.

questions.stem: A news report ends: {電車|でんしゃ}は{一時間|いちじかん}ぐらいおくれるということです。 What does ということです show?
choices: The reporter is guessing from what they see
The trains will certainly be on time
The reporter is asking a question
questions.explanation: 〜ということです at the end of a sentence is a formal "it is reported that", common in news and announcements. A guess from what you see would be 〜ようです or 〜そうです (looks like).

questions.stem: Read: てんきよほうによると、{明日|あした}の{朝|あさ}は{雨|あめ}ですが、{午後|ごご}からはれるそうです。きおんは{二十五度|にじゅうごど}まで{上|あ}がるそうです。でも、{夜|よる}は{風|かぜ}が{強|つよ}くなるそうです。 What will tomorrow night be like?
questions.explanation: {夜|よる}は{風|かぜ}が{強|つよ}くなるそうです: the wind will get strong at night. The rain is in the morning, and the afternoon clears up (はれる); nothing is said about snow.

questions.stem: Match each kanji to its meaning.
questions.explanation: 春 はる spring, 夏 なつ summer, 秋 あき autumn, 冬 ふゆ winter. Wind is 風 (かぜ).

questions.stem: How is 暑い read? {今日|きょう}はとても暑いですね。
questions.explanation: 暑い is あつい, hot weather. さむい is 寒い, cold; くらい (暗い) is dark; あたたかい is warm.

questions.stem: How is 空気 read? {山|やま}の空気はおいしいです。
questions.explanation: 空気 (air) uses the on'yomi クウ + キ: くうき. そら is 空 on its own (sky); から is "empty".

questions.stem: Which kanji is the さむ in さむい (cold weather)?
questions.explanation: 寒 is さむ(い): a roof with ice under it. 暑 is あつ(い), hot weather; 冬 is winter and 風 is wind.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?

audio.text: あしたはあめがふるそうです。

choices: It looks like it will rain tomorrow.
I hear it will rain tomorrow.
questions.explanation: あしたはあめがふるそうです: the dictionary form ふる + そうです is hearsay, "I hear". "Looks like" would be ふりそう, and "might" is かもしれません.

questions.stem: Listen. Is the speaker describing how the cake looks, or passing on something they heard?

audio.text: このケーキ、おいしいそうですよ。

choices: What they guess from the smell
questions.explanation: おいしいそうです keeps the い, so it's hearsay: "I hear it's delicious". How it looks would be おいしそうです.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
tiles: てんきよほうによると、
accept: てんきよほうによると、
questions.prompt: According to the forecast, it'll get cold tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The source (〜によると) usually comes first and hearsay そうです comes last, after the full plain form {寒|さむ}くなる. {明日|あした}は can also come first.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Kenta said he can't come tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The quoted part ({明日|あした}{来|こ}られない) is in the plain form and comes before と; {言|い}っていました comes last. {明日|あした} can also come before けんたさんは.

questions.topic: Seems (ようだ / みたい / らしい)
questions.stem: のどがいたいです。かぜ___ようです。 (My throat hurts. I think I have a cold.)
questions.explanation: A noun takes の before ようだ: かぜのようです. な is for な-adjectives (しずかなようだ), and だ and に never come before ようだ.

questions.topic: Seems (ようだ / みたい / らしい)
questions.stem: Type the casual ending for "seems (from what I can see)": この{店|みせ}、{今日|きょう}は{休|やす}み___。 (Seems it's closed today.)
questions.explanation: みたい joins a noun directly: {休|やす}み + みたい, so you get a double み. The polite equivalent is {休|やす}みのようです.

questions.topic: Seems (ようだ / みたい / らしい)
questions.stem: へやは___ようです。 (The room seems quiet.)
questions.explanation: A な-adjective keeps な before ようだ: しずかなようです. Without な is the みたい pattern (しずかみたい); だ and の don't fit.

questions.topic: Seems (ようだ / みたい / らしい)
questions.stem: You can hear rain on the window. Which sentence fits best?
choices: {雨|あめ}がふったらしいです。
{雨|あめ}がふっているようです。
questions.explanation: You're drawing a conclusion from what you hear right now, so ようだ: ふっているようです, "it seems to be raining". ふりそう is "about to rain" (it already is), ふるそう is hearsay, and ふったらしい is "apparently it rained", from second-hand information.

questions.topic: Seems (ようだ / みたい / らしい)
questions.stem: What does {今日|きょう}は{春|はる}らしい{天気|てんき}ですね。 mean?
choices: I hear it'll be spring weather today.
It looks like the weather will turn to spring.
questions.explanation: Noun + らしい before another noun is "typical of": {春|はる}らしい{天気|てんき}, weather just like spring. "Apparently it's spring" would be {春|はる}らしいです at the end of a sentence, and it makes no sense about the season here.

questions.stem: まるでゆめ___です。 (It's just like a dream.)
questions.explanation: In the sense "just like", まるで goes with ようだ or みたい: まるでゆめのようです (or まるでゆめみたいです). そう can't follow a noun, だそう is hearsay, and らしい doesn't go with まるで.

questions.stem: Which means "big cities such as Tokyo"?
choices: {東京|とうきょう}みたい{大|おお}きい{町|まち}
{東京|とうきょう}らしい{大|おお}きい{町|まち}
{東京|とうきょう}のような{大|おお}きい{町|まち}
{東京|とうきょう}そうな{大|おお}きい{町|まち}
questions.explanation: N のような + noun gives examples: "cities such as Tokyo". みたい before a noun needs な ({東京|とうきょう}みたいな), らしい here would mean "typical of Tokyo", and そう can't follow a noun.

questions.stem: Which is correct for "That person looks young"?
choices: あの{人|ひと}はわかいに{見|み}えます。
あの{人|ひと}はわかく{見|み}えます。
あの{人|ひと}はわかいそうに{見|み}えます。
あの{人|ひと}はわかで{見|み}えます。
questions.explanation: An い-adjective changes い to く before {見|み}える: わかく{見|み}える. に is for な-adjectives and nouns ({元気|げんき}に{見|み}える, {学生|がくせい}に{見|み}える).

questions.stem: {台所|だいどころ}からいい___がします。
questions.explanation: 〜がする is for smells, sounds, voices, tastes and feelings: いいにおいがする, there's a nice smell. Light and shadows are seen ({見|み}える), and {見|み}た{目|め} is looks.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?

audio.text: なにかわすれているきがします。

choices: I have a feeling I've forgotten something.
questions.explanation: 〜{気|き}がする is "I have a feeling (that)". わすれている is the state after forgetting: something has been forgotten. Hearsay would end in そうです.

questions.topic: Seems (ようだ / みたい / らしい)
questions.stem: Which sentence is correct, casual speech?
questions.explanation: みたい joins a な-adjective with nothing between: しずかみたい. な goes with ようだ (しずかなようだ), so ×しずかなみたい mixes the two patterns.

questions.topic: Seems (ようだ / みたい / らしい)
questions.stem: Read: {電気|でんき}がついていて、{台所|だいどころ}からカレーのにおいがします。ドアの{前|まえ}に{父|ちち}のくつがあります。 Which is the best conclusion?
choices: {父|ちち}が{帰|かえ}ってきたようです。
{父|ちち}が{帰|かえ}ってきそうです。
{父|ちち}が{帰|かえ}ってくるそうです。
{父|ちち}が{帰|かえ}ってきたいです。
questions.explanation: From clues you noticed yourself (the light, the smell, the shoes), ようだ: "Dad seems to have come home". きそう is "looks about to come home", くるそう is "I hear he's coming", and きたいです is "want to come home".

questions.stem: How is 明日 read? 明日は{雨|あめ}らしいです。
questions.explanation: 明日 has a special reading, あした (tomorrow): the kanji give the meaning, not the sound. In formal speech it can also be あす or みょうにち, but never めいにち.

questions.stem: How is 真っ赤 read?
questions.explanation: 真っ赤 is まっか (bright red), a special reading: ま + small っ + か. The っ is a full beat of silence.

questions.stem: Which kanji means "dark"?
questions.explanation: 暗 (くら(い)) is dark: the sun next to 音, sound. 明 is bright, 光 is light and 黒 is black.

questions.stem: How is 光って read? あのビルの{上|うえ}で{何|なに}かが光っています。
questions.explanation: 光る (shine) is ひか(る), so 光って is ひかって. コウ is the on'yomi, used in compounds, never with okurigana.

questions.topic: Seems (ようだ / みたい / らしい)
questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?

audio.text: だれかいるみたい。

questions.explanation: だれかいるみたい: いる + みたい, "seems like someone's here", a casual inference. "Wants to" would be いたい, and hearsay would be いるそう.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?

audio.text: いいにおいがしますね。

questions.explanation: いいにおいがしますね: there's a nice smell. においがする is the smell pattern; "looks good" would be おいしそう or よさそう.

questions.topic: Seems (ようだ / みたい / らしい)
questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: The light's on, so someone seems to be in.
questions.explanation: The reason comes first, then the conclusion with ようです at the very end. A verb joins ようだ directly: いるようです; ×いるのようです is wrong (の is only for nouns).

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: The sky is as blue as the sea.
questions.explanation: まるで comes just before the comparison, and N のように goes before the adjective it describes: {海|うみ}のように{青|あお}い. まるで can also open the sentence.

questions.topic: How sure you are (はず / かもしれない)
questions.stem: {明日|あした}は{休|やす}み___はずです。 (Tomorrow should be a holiday.)
questions.explanation: はず is a noun, so a noun before it takes の: {休|やす}みのはずです. な is for な-adjectives (ひまなはず), and だ can't come before はず.

questions.topic: How sure you are (はず / かもしれない)
questions.stem: {日曜日|にちようび}はひま___はずです。 (He should be free on Sunday.)
questions.explanation: A な-adjective keeps な before a noun, and はず is a noun: ひまなはずです. の is for nouns ({休|やす}みのはず).

questions.topic: How sure you are (はず / かもしれない)
questions.stem: あの{人|ひと}は{先生|せんせい}___かもしれません。 (That person might be a teacher.)
questions.explanation: かもしれない joins a noun or な-adjective directly, without だ: {先生|せんせい}かもしれません. ×{先生|せんせい}だかもしれません is a common mistake.

questions.topic: How sure you are (はず / かもしれない)
questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker mean?

audio.text: たなかさんはいまアメリカにいるから、ここにいるはずがありません。

choices: Ms Tanaka can't possibly be here.
Ms Tanaka was supposed to be here.
questions.explanation: はずがない is a strong denial: "there's no way". She's in America, so she can't be here. "Should be" would be いるはずです, and "was supposed to" いるはずでした.

questions.topic: How sure you are (はず / かもしれない)
questions.stem: What happened? バスは{八時|はちじ}に{着|つ}くはずでしたが、おくれました。
choices: The bus arrived at eight as expected.
The bus might arrive at eight.
The bus will surely arrive at eight.
The bus was supposed to arrive at eight, but it was late.
questions.explanation: はずでした (はずだった) is an expectation that didn't come true: "was supposed to". The が、おくれました confirms it: but it was late.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Please hand in the report by Friday"?
choices: レポートは{金曜日|きんようび}まで{出|だ}してください。
レポートは{金曜日|きんようび}までに{出|だ}してください。
レポートは{金曜日|きんようび}からに{出|だ}してください。
レポートは{金曜日|きんようび}の{間|あいだ}{出|だ}してください。
questions.explanation: Handing in happens once, so the deadline takes までに (by). まで (until) is for actions that continue up to a time, like {待|ま}つ or いる.

questions.stem: {五時|ごじ}___ここで{待|ま}っています。 (I'll wait here until five.)
questions.explanation: Waiting goes on the whole time, up to five o'clock, so まで (until). までに would be a deadline for a one-time action, like coming back.

questions.stem: {夏休|なつやす}みの___、{一度|いちど}{国|くに}に{帰|かえ}りました。 (I went home once during the summer holidays.)
questions.explanation: Going home once is a single event inside the period, so {間|あいだ}に. {間|あいだ} alone is for something that lasts the whole time: {夏休|なつやす}みの{間|あいだ}、ずっと{国|くに}にいました.

questions.stem: A sign says {十八|じゅうはっ}さい{以上|いじょう}. Can an eighteen-year-old take part?
choices: Yes: {以上|いじょう} includes eighteen
questions.explanation: {以上|いじょう} includes the number itself: eighteen and over. English "over eighteen" usually excludes eighteen, which is why this is easy to get wrong.

questions.stem: この{店|みせ}は{日曜日|にちようび}{以外|いがい}、{毎日|まいにち}{開|あ}いています。 When is the shop closed?
questions.explanation: {日曜日|にちようび}{以外|いがい} is "except Sunday": it's open every day except Sunday, so it's closed on Sundays. "Every day except Sunday" is when it's open.

questions.topic: How sure you are (はず / かもしれない)
questions.stem: Which sentence is the least certain?
choices: きっと{来|く}るでしょう。
たぶん{来|く}るでしょう。
questions.explanation: かもしれない is only a possibility: "he might come". きっと and はず are near-certain, and たぶん〜でしょう is "probably".

questions.topic: How sure you are (はず / かもしれない)
questions.stem: You have no information, but you want to reassure a friend that tomorrow will be sunny. Which is most natural?
choices: {明日|あした}ははれるはずです。
{明日|あした}ははれるはずがありません。
{明日|あした}はきっとはれますよ。
{明日|あした}ははれるはずでした。
questions.explanation: With no facts to go on, use きっと, which expresses how sure you feel. はず needs a reason you know (a forecast, a timetable), so it sounds odd here; はずがない and はずでした say the opposite.

questions.stem: Read the notice: レポートのしめきりは{七月|しちがつ}{十日|とおか}の{午後|ごご}{五時|ごじ}です。それまでにメールで{送|おく}ってください。{十|じゅっ}ページ{以下|いか}でおねがいします。 Which report follows the rules?
choices: 12 pages, emailed on 10 July at 4 p.m.
8 pages, emailed on 10 July at 6 p.m.
10 pages, handed in on paper on 9 July
8 pages, emailed on 10 July at 4 p.m.
questions.explanation: It must be sent by email (メールで) by 5 p.m. on 10 July (それまでに), and be ten pages or fewer ({以下|いか} includes ten). Twelve pages is too long, 6 p.m. is too late, and paper isn't email.

questions.stem: How is 着きました read? {三時|さんじ}に{駅|えき}に着きました。
questions.explanation: With a place + に, 着く is つく, arrive: つきました. 着 is also き(る), wear, but you don't wear a station; チャク is the on'yomi, never used with okurigana.

questions.stem: How is 間 read here? {電車|でんしゃ}に間に合いました。
questions.explanation: In 間に合う (be in time) 間 is read ま: まにあいました. あいだ is "between, during" and カン is the on'yomi in {時間|じかん}.

questions.stem: Type the reading of 去年 in hiragana: ___
questions.explanation: 去年 (last year) is きょねん: 去 キョ + 年 ネン. N5 wrote the word in kana; now it has its kanji.

questions.topic: How sure you are (はず / かもしれない)
questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?

audio.text: バスはもうすぐくるはずです。

choices: The bus was supposed to come.
questions.explanation: バスはもうすぐくるはずです: はずです is "should", an expectation based on facts like the timetable. "Might" is かもしれません and "can't" はずがありません.

questions.topic: How sure you are (はず / かもしれない)
questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?

audio.text: あしたはあめかもしれません。

choices: I hear it will rain tomorrow.
questions.explanation: あしたはあめかもしれません: a noun + かもしれません, "it might be rain". "I hear" would be あめだそうです, and "surely" きっと.

questions.topic: How sure you are (はず / かもしれない)
questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Mr Yamada took the nine o'clock train, so he should arrive soon.
questions.explanation: The reason (〜から) comes first, then the expectation with はず at the end, after the plain form {着|つ}く. はずが would make はずがない, the opposite meaning.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: I read a book the whole time I was waiting for the train.
questions.explanation: Reading went on the whole time, so 〜ている{間|あいだ} (not までに, which is a deadline). The time clause comes first and the main verb {読|よ}んでいました last.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Do you know what time the film starts?"
choices: {映画|えいが}が{何時|なんじ}に{始|はじ}まりますか{知|し}っていますか。
{映画|えいが}が{何時|なんじ}に{始|はじ}まるか{知|し}っていますか。
{映画|えいが}が{何時|なんじ}に{始|はじ}まる{知|し}っていますか。
{映画|えいが}が{何時|なんじ}に{始|はじ}まるかどうか{知|し}っていますか。
questions.explanation: The inner question is in the plain form and keeps its か: {始|はじ}まるか. ます doesn't go inside, the か can't be dropped, and かどうか is only for yes/no questions, not ones with a question word like {何時|なんじ}.

questions.stem: {明日|あした}{来|く}る___、まだ{分|わ}かりません。 (I don't know yet whether he's coming tomorrow.)
questions.explanation: A yes/no question inside a sentence takes かどうか, "whether": {来|く}るかどうか. かな (I wonder) ends a sentence by itself, and のは makes a topic, not a question.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Do you know who that person is?"
choices: あの{人|ひと}がだれですか{知|し}っていますか。
あの{人|ひと}がだれのか{知|し}っていますか。
あの{人|ひと}がだれを{知|し}っていますか。
あの{人|ひと}がだれか{知|し}っていますか。
questions.explanation: だ (and です) drops before か in an indirect question: だれか{知|し}っていますか. ですか can't stay inside, and だれを would change the meaning to "whom does that person know".

questions.topic: Something and someone (なにか / だれか)
questions.stem: 「{何|なに}か{食|た}べましたか。」 Which is the natural "No, I didn't eat anything"?
choices: いいえ、{何|なに}か{食|た}べませんでした。
いいえ、{何|なに}も{食|た}べませんでした。
いいえ、{何|なに}でも{食|た}べませんでした。
いいえ、{何|なに}を{食|た}べませんでした。
questions.explanation: {何|なに}か is for questions and positive sentences; with a negative verb, "nothing" is {何|なに}も. {何|なに}でも is "anything at all" and doesn't go with a negative like this.

questions.topic: Something and someone (なにか / だれか)
questions.stem: Which sentence means "I want to go somewhere"?
choices: どこかに{行|い}きたいです。
どこにも{行|い}きたいです。
どこか{行|い}きたくないです。
どこへ{行|い}きたいですか。
questions.explanation: どこか is "somewhere", and particles like に stay after it: どこかに{行|い}きたい. どこにも goes with a negative ("nowhere"), and どこへ…ですか asks where.

questions.stem: Listen. Someone says this to themselves. What are they doing?

audio.text: あしたは、はれるかな。

choices: Saying it will definitely be sunny
Wondering whether it will be sunny tomorrow
questions.explanation: Plain form + かな is "I wonder…", said mostly to yourself or to friends. A report would use そうだ, and the polite version to a teacher would be 〜でしょうか.

questions.stem: You want to wonder aloud, politely, to your teacher: "I wonder if the rain will stop." Which is best?
questions.explanation: 〜でしょうか is the polite "I wonder". かな is casual, かしら sounds dated and feminine, and って is casual hearsay ("they say it'll stop").

questions.stem: Type the missing kana: 「{田中|たなか}さんが{来|き}たんですか。」「いいえ、{来|き}た___は{山田|やまだ}さんです。」
questions.explanation: The 〜のは〜だ pattern turns {来|き}た into a noun with の: {来|き}たのは{山田|やまだ}さんです, "the one who came was Mr Yamada". It puts the corrected part, {山田|やまだ}さん, at the end.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I forgot to turn the light off"?
choices: {電気|でんき}をけすをわすれました。
{電気|でんき}がけすのをわすれました。
{電気|でんき}をけしてわすれました。
{電気|でんき}をけすのをわすれました。
questions.explanation: To forget to do something, add の after the verb: けすのをわすれる. A verb can't take を directly, and {電気|でんき}が would make the light the one doing the turning off.

questions.stem: You want to ask a station worker, politely, when the next bus comes. Which is best?
choices: つぎのバスは{何時|なんじ}に{来|く}るか、{教|おし}えていただけませんか。
つぎのバスは{何時|なんじ}に{来|き}ますか{教|おし}えてくれ。
つぎのバスが{何時|なんじ}か{来|く}る、{教|おし}えてください。
つぎのバスが{来|く}るかどうか{何時|なんじ}、{教|おし}えて。
questions.explanation: The indirect question is plain ({来|く}るか), and 〜ていただけませんか is the polite request from lesson 7. The others put ます inside, use the rough 〜てくれ, or scramble the question word.

questions.stem: At the lost-property office: {黒|くろ}くて{小|ちい}さいリュックです。なかみは{青|あお}いさいふと{本|ほん}です。 What did the speaker lose?
choices: A big blue backpack with a black wallet in it
A small black backpack with a blue wallet and a book in it
A small black wallet with a blue book in it
A blue bag with a black book inside
questions.explanation: {黒|くろ}くて{小|ちい}さいリュック is a small black backpack; なかみ (contents) are a blue wallet and a book. The colours belong to different things, which is the trap.

questions.stem: At a counter, you want to speak to the person in charge. Which do you ask for?
questions.explanation: かかりの{人|ひと} is the person in charge. {知|し}り{合|あ}い is an acquaintance, あんないじょ an information office and パンフレット a brochure.

questions.stem: よく___ください。 (Please think it over carefully.)
questions.explanation: {考|かんが}える is thinking something through, so よく{考|かんが}えてください. {思|おも}う is having an opinion or a feeling, which you can't do "carefully" on request; {思|おも}い{出|だ}す is remember and {知|し}らせる is let someone know.

questions.stem: How is 問題 read? 問題ありません。
questions.explanation: 問題 is もんだい: モン + ダイ. 問題ありません is "no problem". と(う) is the kun'yomi of 問, used in {問|と}い{合|あ}わせ.

questions.stem: Which kanji is the こた of こたえる (to answer)?
questions.explanation: 答 is こた(える): bamboo over 合, the answer that fits. 問 is ask, 題 topic, and 考 think.

questions.stem: How is 知らせて read? {着|つ}いたら知らせてください。
questions.explanation: 知らせる (let someone know) is しらせる, from し(る): しらせて. チ is the on'yomi, and お{知|し}らせ (a notice) is the noun.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker ask?

audio.text: なんじにはじまるかしっていますか。

choices: Do you know whether it starts?
Do you know what time it starts?
I don't know when it starts.
Did it start at the usual time?
questions.explanation: なんじにはじまるかしっていますか: an indirect question with {何時|なんじ}, inside しっていますか. "Whether" would be はじまるかどうか.

questions.topic: Something and someone (なにか / だれか)
questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?

audio.text: なにかのみませんか。

choices: Would you like something to drink?
questions.explanation: なにかのみませんか: {何|なに}か (something) + のみませんか, an invitation. "What" would be なにをのみますか, and "anything" with a negative is なにも.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Excuse me, please tell me where to change trains.
questions.explanation: The indirect question (どこでのりかえるか, plain form + か) comes before {教|おし}えてください. ます can't go inside: ×のりかえますか.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: I don't know yet whether he's coming tomorrow.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question inside a sentence is plain form + かどうか: {明日|あした}{来|く}るかどうか. まだ can go just before {分|わ}かりません or at the very start.

questions.stem: A headline reads {大雨|おおあめ}で{電車|でんしゃ}とまる. What does it report?
choices: Trains stopped because of heavy rain
Trains will stop if it rains heavily
It rained heavily on the trains
The heavy rain may stop tomorrow
questions.explanation: Headlines drop が and often use the dictionary form for something that has already happened: {電車|でんしゃ}(が)とまる = the trains stopped. で gives the cause: because of heavy rain.

questions.stem: In the headline {市|し}の{図書館|としょかん}、{日曜日|にちようび}も{開|あ}く, which particle does the comma stand for?
questions.explanation: The full sentence is {市|し}の{図書館|としょかん}は{日曜日|にちようび}も{開|あ}きます: the comma replaces the topic は. Headlines drop は, が and を to save space.

questions.stem: What does the か at the end of {夜|よる}の{火事|かじ}　{台所|だいどころ}から{火|ひ}か mean?
choices: It's a question to the reader
The cause is thought likely but not confirmed
The fire definitely started in the kitchen
A fire will start in the kitchen
questions.explanation: か at the end of a headline means "possibly, it's thought": the fire may have started in the kitchen, but this isn't confirmed. It isn't a question to the reader.

questions.stem: Which is the formal written version of {雨|あめ}だった?
questions.explanation: である replaces だ, so だった becomes であった. {雨|あめ}でした is the polite spoken form, not the written style.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT correct in the written だ/である style?
choices: {町|まち}は{大|おお}きいである。
はんにんは{男|おとこ}である。
questions.explanation: である only replaces だ after nouns and な-adjectives. An い-adjective never takes だ, so it never takes である either: just {町|まち}は{大|おお}きい.

questions.stem: In a news report, which ending marks the words of someone who was interviewed?
questions.explanation: 「…」と{話|はな}していました introduces what an interviewee said. ということです is reported information in general, はっぴょうしました is used for organisations announcing something, and である is just the written copula.

questions.stem: Why do news reports rarely end with らしい?
choices: It's a casual form of です
It sounds second-hand and doesn't name a source
questions.explanation: らしい sounds like something picked up second-hand, with no named source, so reporters prefer 〜によると…そうだ or ということだ. In conversation about the news, らしい is fine.

questions.stem: In the lesson's article, why did the students make the map?
choices: Many visitors got lost on the way from the station
The old map was only in English
Their teacher asked them to in winter
questions.explanation: {駅|えき}からの{道|みち}が{分|わ}かりにくくて、まよう{人|ひと}が{多|おお}い: the way from the station was hard to follow and many people got lost. The map has shops in it, and it's new, in Japanese and English.

questions.stem: In the article, where can visitors get the map?
questions.explanation: {駅|えき}のあんないじょでもらうことができます: you can get it at the station information office.

questions.stem: In the article, when did the students make the map?
questions.explanation: {夏休|なつやす}みの{間|あいだ}に{町|まち}を{歩|ある}いて: they walked round the town during the summer holidays. Autumn is when many visitors come.

questions.stem: Type the word for "the police" in hiragana: ___
questions.explanation: けいさつ (the police). Its kanji are outside N4, so this course writes it in kana.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the news say?

audio.text: けいさつによると、けがをしたひとはいないそうです。

choices: According to the police, nobody was hurt.
According to the police, someone was hurt.
questions.explanation: けいさつによると、けがをしたひとはいないそうです: according to the police (によると), there's nobody who was hurt (いない), and そうです marks it as reported.

questions.stem: Which おみくじ rank is the best?
questions.explanation: {大吉|だいきち} is great luck, the top rank. {小吉|しょうきち} and {末吉|すえきち} are lesser luck (their order varies by shrine), and {凶|きょう} is bad luck.

questions.stem: You draw {凶|きょう} (bad luck). What do many people do with the slip?
choices: Tie it to a rack or branch at the shrine
Keep it in their wallet for a year
questions.explanation: A common custom is to tie a bad fortune up at the shrine and leave the bad luck behind. Keeping it in your wallet is what many people do with a good one.

questions.stem: Which ろくよう day is the most popular for weddings?
questions.explanation: {大安|たいあん} is the luckiest day and the most popular for weddings. {仏滅|ぶつめつ} is the unluckiest, and {赤口|しゃっこう} is unlucky except around noon.

questions.stem: How is 大安 read?
questions.explanation: 大安 is たいあん, with た, not だ: a reading worth learning because だいあん is a common mistake.

questions.stem: On which day are funerals usually avoided?
questions.explanation: {友引|ともびき} "pulls a friend along", so funerals are avoided that day and many crematoriums close. It's weddings that avoid {仏滅|ぶつめつ}.

questions.stem: What is a まねきねこ said to do?
questions.explanation: The まねきねこ (beckoning cat) raises a paw to invite customers and money into a shop. Which paw means what is explained in different ways.

questions.stem: Why are the numbers 4 and 9 avoided in some hospitals and hotels?
choices: They are only unlucky in China
They look like the kanji for ghost
し and く sound like the words for death and suffering
questions.explanation: The readings し (4) and く (9) sound like the words for death and suffering, so some places skip room numbers 4 and 9, and gifts aren't usually given in fours.

questions.stem: You want to describe a belief without stating it as a fact. Which is best?
choices: {八|はち}はえんぎがいいです。
{八|はち}はえんぎがいいと{言|い}われています。
{八|はち}はえんぎがいいはずです。
{八|はち}はえんぎがよさそうです。
questions.explanation: 〜と{言|い}われています (it is said) reports the belief without claiming it. The plain sentence states it as fact, はず claims a reasoned expectation, and よさそう is "looks lucky".

questions.stem: Type the word for "fortune slip" (from a shrine or temple) in hiragana: ___
questions.explanation: おみくじ: a paper slip with your fortune, drawn at a shrine or temple. おみくじを{引|ひ}く is "draw a fortune slip".

questions.stem: In the dialogue, Sota says {凶|きょう}って、あまり{出|で}ないらしいよ。 What does he mean?
choices: Apparently bad luck rarely comes up.
Bad luck will surely come up.
He hopes bad luck won't come up.
Bad luck looks likely to come up.
questions.explanation: らしい marks something he has heard: "apparently". あまり〜ない is "not often". "Looks likely" would be 〜そう, and "surely" きっと.

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say?

audio.text: きょうはうんがいいかもしれません。

choices: I hear I'll be lucky today.
questions.explanation: きょうはうんがいいかもしれません: {運|うん}がいい (lucky) + かもしれません (might). "I hear" would be いいそうです, and "certainly" きっと.

questions.stem: What does えんぎがいい mean?
questions.explanation: えんぎ is an omen, so えんぎがいい is "a good sign, lucky" and えんぎがわるい "a bad sign". Good health is けんこう.

questions.stem: What is the passive of {書|か}く (to write)?
questions.explanation: Group 1 verbs move to the あ row and add れる: か → か + れる, {書|か}かれる. {書|か}かせる is the causative (lesson 22), and {書|か}けれる mixes the え row of the potential ({書|か}ける) with れる.

questions.stem: What is the passive of {言|い}う (to say)?
questions.explanation: Verbs ending in う take わ, not あ, before れる, just as their ない form is {言|い}わない: {言|い}われる. 言あれる is the tempting "あ row" mistake, and {言|い}わせる is the causative.

questions.stem: Type the passive of {来|く}る (to come): ___
questions.explanation: {来|く}る → {来|こ}られる, read こられる, the same shape as its potential. It's used mostly as a suffering passive: {友|とも}だちに{来|こ}られた (a friend turned up, unwelcome). くられる and きられる are not forms of {来|く}る.

questions.stem: Read: 「{弟|おとうと}は{父|ちち}にしかられました。」 Who did the scolding?
choices: Father and my brother scolded me.
questions.explanation: In a passive, に marks the agent, the one who acts: {父|ちち}に, so Father scolded. The subject {弟|おとうと}は is the one it happened to. Reading に as "to" gives the reversed meaning.

questions.stem: Choose the particle: 「{私|わたし}は{先生|せんせい}___ほめられました。」 (I was praised by the teacher.)
questions.explanation: The agent of a passive takes に: {先生|せんせい}にほめられました. を would make the teacher the one praised, and が would make the teacher the subject, which clashes with {私|わたし}は.

questions.stem: Which sentence is the most natural way to say "Someone stepped on my foot on the train"?
choices: {電車|でんしゃ}で{私|わたし}の{足|あし}がふまれました。
{電車|でんしゃ}で{足|あし}をふまれました。
{電車|でんしゃ}で{足|あし}にふまれました。
{電車|でんしゃ}で{足|あし}をふみました。
questions.explanation: When something happens to part of you, you (unspoken) are the subject and the body part keeps を: {足|あし}をふまれました. {私|わたし}の{足|あし}がふまれました is understandable but sounds like a report about the foot. {足|あし}に makes the foot the one who stepped, and ふみました means I stepped.

questions.stem: What does 「{雨|あめ}にふられました。」 mean?
choices: I got caught in the rain.
I like walking in the rain.
questions.explanation: This is the suffering passive of ふる: the speaker was rained on and was affected (got wet, plans spoiled). A plain report that it rained would be {雨|あめ}がふりました.

questions.stem: Read: 「{弟|おとうと}にケーキを{食|た}べられました。」 How does the speaker feel?
choices: Happy that the brother enjoyed the cake.
Proud that the brother made a cake.
Surprised that the brother can eat cake.
Annoyed: the brother ate the speaker's cake.
questions.explanation: The suffering passive says the speaker was affected, nearly always unpleasantly: the brother ate the cake, and the speaker minds. Happiness would be expressed differently, for example {食|た}べてくれました. "Can eat" would be the potential with が: ケーキが{食|た}べられる.

questions.stem: Read: 「{私|わたし}は{生|なま}の{魚|さかな}が{食|た}べられます。」 What does it mean?
choices: I am eaten by raw fish.
I was made to eat raw fish.
Raw fish is eaten in my country.
questions.explanation: For group 2 verbs the potential and passive look the same. Here {魚|さかな}が marks what can be eaten, and there's no agent with に, so it's the potential: I can eat raw fish. "Was made to eat" would be {食|た}べさせられました.

questions.stem: In writing, which fits best? 「この{本|ほん}は{有名|ゆうめい}な{先生|せんせい}＿＿＿{書|か}かれました。」 (This book was written by a famous teacher.)
questions.explanation: For the creator of something built, written, invented or discovered, the agent takes によって. を and が don't mark an agent at all, and で would mean "at" or "by means of".

questions.stem: What does 「このしろは{日本|にほん}でいちばん{古|ふる}いと{言|い}われています。」 mean?
choices: I was told off for saying this castle is old.
Someone told me this castle isn't old.
This castle is said to be the oldest in Japan.
This castle is called "the Old Castle".
questions.explanation: 〜と{言|い}われている is "it is said that": a belief many people hold, reported without the speaker vouching for it. It's not about one person telling the speaker something, which would be 〜と{言|い}われました.

questions.stem: How is 世界 read in 「{英語|えいご}は世界{中|じゅう}で{使|つか}われています。」?
questions.explanation: 世界 is せかい (world): 世 is read セ here, not セイ, and 界 is カイ. 世界中 (せかいじゅう) means "all over the world".

questions.stem: Which kanji means "bird"?
questions.explanation: 鳥 (とり) is a picture of a bird, with four dots for its feet or tail at the bottom. 犬 is dog, 池 is pond, 建 is build.

questions.stem: How is 有名 read in 「このしろは有名です。」?
questions.explanation: 有 is ユウ and 名 is メイ: ゆうめい (famous). 有 is also read ウ in a few words, but not here, and あ(る) is its kun'yomi, which isn't used in compounds.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
questions.explanation: {鳥|とり} bird, {犬|いぬ} dog, さる monkey, ぞう elephant, むし insect. A cat is ねこ.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: My little brother ate my cake (and I'm annoyed).
questions.explanation: {私|わたし}は{弟|おとうと}にケーキを{食|た}べられてしまいました. The sufferer is the subject, the brother is the agent with に, the cake keeps を, and the passive {食|た}べられて + しまいました adds regret. {弟|おとうと}に and ケーキを can swap. {食|た}べさせて would mean I made him eat it.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: This building was built a hundred years ago.
questions.explanation: この{建物|たてもの}は{百年|ひゃくねん}{前|まえ}に{建|た}てられました. The building is the subject, so the verb is the passive {建|た}てられました; {建|た}てました would need a person as the subject. The time can also come first.

questions.stem: Listen. What happened to the speaker?

audio.text: でんしゃでさいふをぬすまれました。

choices: They stole a wallet on the train.
They found a wallet on the train.
Their wallet was stolen on the train.
questions.explanation: ぬすまれました is the passive of ぬすむ (to steal): the speaker had their wallet stolen. "They stole" would be ぬすみました, and "found" would be みつけました.

questions.stem: Listen and type the verb you hear, in hiragana: ___

audio.text: ほめられました

questions.explanation: ほめられました: the polite past of ほめられる, the passive of ほめる (to praise). "I was praised."

questions.stem: Listen. When was the castle built?

audio.text: このしろは、よんひゃくねんまえにたてられました。

questions.explanation: よんひゃくねんまえ is 400 years ago. Forty would be よんじゅうねん, four thousand よんせんねん, and a hundred and forty ひゃくよんじゅうねん.

questions.stem: What is the causative of {書|か}く (to write)?
questions.explanation: Group 1: あ row + せる, {書|か}かせる. {書|か}かれる is the passive (れる, not せる), and 〜させる is only for group 2 verbs, so {書|か}きさせる is wrong.

questions.stem: What is the causative of {話|はな}す (to speak)?
questions.explanation: す → さ + せる: {話|はな}させる (はな-さ-せる). {話|はな}せる is the potential ("can speak"), the tempting mistake when the さ is dropped.

questions.stem: Type the causative of {食|た}べる (to eat): ___
questions.explanation: Group 2 verbs drop る and add させる: {食|た}べさせる. {食|た}べせる is missing the さ.

questions.stem: Type the causative of {来|く}る (to come): ___
questions.explanation: {来|く}る → {来|こ}させる, read こさせる, with the こ of {来|こ}ない. きさせる and くらせる aren't forms of {来|く}る.

questions.stem: Choose the particle: 「{母|はは}は{弟|おとうと}＿＿＿{野菜|やさい}を{食|た}べさせました。」
questions.explanation: The verb already has a を object ({野菜|やさい}を), so the person made to act takes に. A second を for {弟|おとうと} would give two を for one verb, which Japanese avoids.

questions.stem: Choose the particle: 「{友|とも}だち＿＿＿{一時間|いちじかん}も{待|ま}たせてしまいました。」 (I kept my friend waiting a whole hour.)
questions.explanation: {待|ま}たせる (keep someone waiting) takes the person with を: {友|とも}だちを{待|ま}たせた. が would make the friend the one doing the making, and と would mean "with my friend".

questions.stem: What does 「{父|ちち}は{私|わたし}に{車|くるま}を{運転|うんてん}させてくれました。」 mean?
choices: Father made me drive the car against my will.
I let Father drive the car.
Father kindly let me drive the car.
Father drove me somewhere in the car.
questions.explanation: The causative + くれる is always "let", with gratitude: Father let me drive. "Against my will" would be the causative-passive (lesson 23), and "I let Father" would need {私|わたし}が as the subject and {父|ちち}に.

questions.stem: You want to ask your boss, very politely, whether you may go home early. What do you say?
choices: {早|はや}く{帰|かえ}らせていただきます。
{早|はや}く{帰|かえ}ってください。
{早|はや}く{帰|かえ}らせましょうか。
{早|はや}く{帰|かえ}らせていただけませんか。
questions.explanation: 〜させていただけませんか asks to be allowed, very politely. 〜させていただきます announces what you're going to do rather than asking, {帰|かえ}ってください tells the boss to go home, and {帰|かえ}らせましょうか offers to send someone home.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "Let me think about it a little"?
choices: {少|すこ}し{考|かんが}えさせてください。
{少|すこ}し{考|かんが}えてください。
{少|すこ}し{考|かんが}えられてください。
{少|すこ}し{考|かんが}えさせられてください。
questions.explanation: The causative て form + ください is "please let me": {考|かんが}えさせてください. {考|かんが}えてください asks the other person to think. The passive and causative-passive versions make no sense as requests.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I made my parents worry"?
choices: {親|おや}にしんぱいされてしまいました。
{親|おや}をしんぱいさせてしまいました。
{親|おや}がしんぱいさせてしまいました。
{親|おや}をしんぱいしてしまいました。
questions.explanation: With feelings, the causative means "make someone feel", and the person takes を: {親|おや}をしんぱいさせた. {親|おや}にしんぱいされた is the passive (my parents worried about me), and {親|おや}をしんぱいした means I worried about my parents.

questions.stem: Which sentence most clearly means "let", not "make"?
choices: {子|こ}どもにゲームをやめさせました。
{子|こ}どもに{野菜|やさい}を{食|た}べさせました。
{子|こ}どもに{好|す}きなだけゲームをさせてあげました。
{子|こ}どもにしゅくだいをさせました。
questions.explanation: {好|す}きなだけ (as much as they liked) and 〜させてあげる make it clear the child was allowed to. Stopping a game, eating vegetables and doing homework are things a parent usually makes a child do.

questions.stem: How is 働 read in 「{毎日|まいにち}{夜|よる}まで働いています。」?
questions.explanation: {働|はたら}く (to work): 働いています is はたらいています. うご(く) is 動 (move), which 働 contains; ドウ is 働's on'yomi, not used in this verb.

questions.stem: How is 会社員 read?
questions.explanation: 員 is イン (member): {会社|かいしゃ} + 員 = かいしゃいん, office worker. 員 is never read ニン; that's a reading of 人.

questions.stem: Which kanji is used to write つく(る), "to make"?
questions.explanation: {作|つく}る. 使 is つか(う) (use), 働 is はたら(く) (work), and 主 is おも (main).

questions.stem: How is 主に read in 「この{店|みせ}では主に{学生|がくせい}が{働|はたら}いています。」?
questions.explanation: 主に is おもに (mainly), with the kun'yomi おも. シュ is the on'yomi in {主人|しゅじん}, and ぬし is a different kun'yomi (owner), not used here.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: My mother made me tidy my room.
questions.explanation: {母|はは}は{私|わたし}にへやをかたづけさせました. かたづける has its own object (へやを), so the person made to act takes に, not を. {私|わたし}に and へやを can swap.

questions.stem: Build the request in Japanese.
questions.prompt: Excuse me, could I possibly take tomorrow off work?
questions.explanation: すみません、{明日|あした}{会社|かいしゃ}を{休|やす}ませていただけませんか. The causative {休|やす}ませて + いただけませんか asks to be allowed. {休|やす}んでいただけませんか would ask the boss to take the day off.

questions.stem: Listen. Who wrote the essays?

audio.text: せんせいはがくせいにさくぶんをかかせました。

questions.explanation: かかせました is the causative: the teacher (は) made the students (に) write. The person on に is the one who does the writing.

questions.stem: Listen and type the verb you hear, in hiragana: ___

audio.text: いかせました

questions.explanation: いかせました, the polite past of {行|い}かせる, the causative of {行|い}く: (someone) made or let someone go.

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker doing?

audio.text: きょうは、はやくかえらせていただきます。

choices: Announcing that they will leave early today
Asking whether they may leave early today
Telling someone else to go home early
Complaining that they were sent home early
questions.explanation: 〜させていただきます announces what the speaker is going to do, as if with the listener's permission. A question would be 〜させていただけませんか, and a complaint about being sent home would use the causative-passive (かえらされました).

questions.stem: What is the causative-passive of {食|た}べる (to eat)?
questions.explanation: Causative {食|た}べさせる + passive 〜られる = {食|た}べさせられる. The short される form exists only for group 1 verbs, so {食|た}べさされる is wrong; {食|た}べさせる is the plain causative.

questions.stem: What is the everyday (short) causative-passive of {書|か}く (to write)?
questions.explanation: Group 1: あ row + される, {書|か}かされる (the long form is {書|か}かせられる). {書|か}かれる is the passive, "be written", and {書|か}かせる is the causative.

questions.stem: What is the causative-passive of {話|はな}す (to speak)?
questions.explanation: Verbs in す have only the long form: {話|はな}させる + られる = {話|はな}させられる. The short form would give さされる, two さ in a row, which Japanese avoids. {話|はな}される is the plain passive.

questions.stem: Type the causative-passive of {待|ま}つ (to wait): ___ (be kept waiting)
questions.explanation: {待|ま}たされる (short, everyday) or {待|ま}たせられる (long): あ row た + される. {待|ま}たれる would be the plain passive.

questions.stem: Type the causative-passive of する: ___
questions.explanation: させる (causative) + られる = させられる: "be made to do". There's no short form for する.

questions.stem: Listen. What happened?

audio.text: わたしは、あににうたわされました。

choices: I made my older brother sing.
My older brother sang for me.
My older brother made me sing.
My older brother praised my singing.
questions.explanation: The speaker said わたしは、あににうたわされました. In a causative-passive the subject is the one made to act ({私|わたし}は), and に marks the one who made them ({兄|あに}に). "I made my brother sing" would be the causative {兄|あに}に{歌|うた}わせました.

questions.stem: Which sentence shows that the speaker was glad?
choices: {父|ちち}に{車|くるま}を{洗|あら}わされました。
{父|ちち}に{車|くるま}を{運転|うんてん}させられました。
{父|ちち}に{車|くるま}を{洗|あら}われました。
{父|ちち}に{車|くるま}を{運転|うんてん}させてもらいました。
questions.explanation: 〜させてもらう means "was allowed to", gratefully. The causative-passive ({洗|あら}わされました, {運転|うんてん}させられました) means the speaker was made to and didn't want to. {洗|あら}われました is the plain passive.

questions.stem: Choose the particle: 「{私|わたし}は{先生|せんせい}＿＿＿{作文|さくぶん}を{書|か}かされました。」
questions.explanation: The one who made it happen takes に, as in every passive: {先生|せんせい}に. The essay already has を, and が would clash with {私|わたし}は as the subject.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "This book is written in English"?
choices: この{本|ほん}は{英語|えいご}で{書|か}かされています。
この{本|ほん}は{英語|えいご}で{書|か}かれています。
この{本|ほん}は{英語|えいご}で{書|か}かせています。
この{本|ほん}は{英語|えいご}で{書|か}けています。
questions.explanation: "Is written" is the passive, {書|か}かれる. {書|か}かされる is "be made to write", which a book can't be, and {書|か}かせる is "make someone write".

questions.stem: Which of these forms is NOT correct Japanese?
questions.explanation: Only group 1 verbs (except those in す) have the short される form. {食|た}べる is group 2, so its only causative-passive is {食|た}べさせられる. The other three are all correct.

questions.stem: Read: 「{子|こ}どものころ、{母|はは}に{毎日|まいにち}ピアノをれんしゅうさせられました。いやでしたが、{今|いま}はよかったと{思|おも}っています。」 How does the speaker feel now?
choices: Keen to give up the piano
Glad they were made to practise
questions.explanation: The causative-passive and いやでした show the speaker didn't want to practise as a child, but {今|いま}はよかったと {思|おも}っています says they're glad now.

questions.stem: How is 漢字 read in 「{毎日|まいにち}漢字を{書|か}かされました。」?
questions.explanation: 漢 is カン and 字 is ジ: かんじ. かじ (without the ん) is a different word, a fire.

questions.stem: How is 試合 read in 「{明日|あした}は試合があります。」?
questions.explanation: 試合 is しあい (match, game): 試 is シ and 合 is read あい here. ため(す) is 試's kun'yomi, used in the verb {試|ため}す.

questions.stem: How is 作文 read?
questions.explanation: 作 is サク and 文 is ブン: さくぶん (essay). モン is a rarer reading of 文, and つく(る) is 作's kun'yomi, not used in this compound.

questions.stem: Which word is written 試験?
questions.explanation: 試験 is しけん, exam. しあい is 試合, えいご is 英語, and かんじ is 漢字.

questions.stem: Match each verb to its causative-passive.
questions.explanation: Group 1 (not す): あ row + される ({書|か}かされる, {飲|の}まされる). Verbs in す, group 2 and する take the long 〜させられる. {話|はな}さされる isn't a correct form.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: I was kept waiting a whole hour at the station.
questions.explanation: {私|わたし}は{駅|えき}で{一時間|いちじかん}も{待|ま}たされました. {待|ま}たされる (be kept waiting) is the causative-passive of {待|ま}つ; も after a quantity stresses how long it was. {待|ま}たれました is the plain passive.

questions.stem: Build the sentence in Japanese.
questions.prompt: As a child, I was made to eat vegetables by my mother.
questions.explanation: {子|こ}どものころ、{母|はは}に{野菜|やさい}を{食|た}べさせられました. The one who made me takes に, the vegetables keep を, and the verb is the causative-passive. {食|た}べさせました would mean I made someone eat them.

questions.stem: Listen. What was the speaker made to do?

audio.text: まいあさ、はちじまえにがっこうにこさせられました。

choices: Come to school before eight every morning
Leave school at eight every evening
Come to school at eight at night
questions.explanation: こさせられました is the causative-passive of {来|く}る: the speaker was made to come. まいあさ is every morning, and はちじまえに is before eight.

questions.stem: Listen. Which form did you hear?

audio.text: かかされました

choices: かかされました (was made to write)
かかせました (made someone write)
questions.explanation: The speaker said かかされました, with さ before れ: the causative-passive. The passive かかれました has no さ, and the causative かかせました has せ but no れ.

questions.stem: Choose the right words: 「{日本語|にほんご}のニュースが{分|わ}かる___なりました。」 (I can now understand the news in Japanese.)
questions.explanation: Dictionary form + ようになる describes a change: "I've come to understand". ために is "in order to" and can't go before なる here; ようで and のに don't fit the pattern.

questions.stem: Which sentence means "I make a point of walking every morning"?
choices: {毎朝|まいあさ}{歩|ある}くようになっています。
{毎朝|まいあさ}{歩|ある}くようにしています。
{毎朝|まいあさ}{歩|ある}くためにしています。
{毎朝|まいあさ}{歩|ある}くのにしています。
